items.title: Olu of Warri’s fifth Anniversary: It’s about culture, homecoming, empowerment – Lawrence Wilbert
items.description: As the Olu of Warri, Ogiame Atuwatse III, marks his fifth year on the throne, activities are being held across the kingdom to celebrate the anniversary and promote the culture, identity and development of the Itsekiri people. In this interview, the Agura Tete of Warri Kingdom, Chief Lawrence Wilbert, speaks on the significance of the anniversary, the Olu’s vision for Warri Kingdom, the preservation of Itsekiri language and culture, inter-ethnic relations in the Niger Delta, and the potential of Warri as a hub for blue economy. By Charles Kumolu, Deputy Editor The Olu of Warri, Ogiame Atuwatse lll, is celebrating his fifth year on the throne… The formal programme started on August 17, with activities highlighting what Ogiame has been able to achieve this year with the Global Homecoming of Itsekiri people. That was preceded by an Itsekiri language competition involving children, which is part of the efforts to promote the language among the younger generation. There were also a series of activities taking place across the kingdom before the formal programme. One of these is the Benin River Life series of events, which takes place on August 15. There are also activities involving gospel artistes and other programmes. There was also a novelty football match on August 20. What does the fifth coronation anniversary mean to the Itsekiri people? The king lives forever. Five years is a landmark, and His Majesty, Ogiame Atuwatse III, is someone who makes sure that his family, his children and his subjects are involved in everything that will bring life and progress to them. For the fifth coronation anniversary, he considered it an opportunity for Itsekiri people all over the world to return home. It is not limited to Itsekiri alone. It includes friends of Itsekiri and everyone who has blood ties to Itsekiri. His Majesty is looking forward to personally welcoming them and participating in events with them. It has so far been a grand occasion. The anniversary provides an opportunity to say that, after five years of building, this is the time to come together once again and celebrate as a people. We have a history and a traditional institution that goes back more than 500 years. That heritage cannot simply be written away. There was a period when people lost confidence in who they were, but today, the Itsekiri are becoming increasingly confident in their identity, particularly with a king like Ogiame Atuwatse III on the throne.The future is bright. Beyond culture and tradition, what would you say has been the major focus of the Olu in the last five years? I am not talking only about culture and tradition only. I am talking about the livelihood of the ordinary Itsekiri person. For at least the past two years, His Majesty has focused increasingly on what is happening to his people economically. We are a people who sit on the wealth that feeds Nigeria from an economic perspective, particularly through the oil and gas industry, yet we remain among the poorest. His Majesty has been addressing that reality. Thankfully, the Petroleum Industry Act has also been implemented over these years. Beyond that, His Majesty has focused on cultural diplomacy, engaging not only the ethnic nationalities around us and across Nigeria, but also traditional institutions and ethnic nationalities in different parts of Africa. He is part of a broader conversation about the renaissance of African identity and the recognition of the leadership role Africa should play in the world. For the Itsekiri, it is exciting to be part of that process. Africa is coming into its own, and His Majesty has been working towards that. I think this fifth coronation anniversary is an opportunity to bring all those efforts together and showcase that we are a humble people, but we know who we are and we are ready for the world. A few years ago, the Olu instituted awards such as the Royal Order of Iwere, ROl, What special activities or initiatives should people expect during this anniversary? His Majesty has the prerogative to determine what he wants to present and showcase to the rest of the world. But what is important is that we want to demonstrate that all the work that has been done in human capacity development and the repositioning of Warri Kingdom is beginning to bear fruit. Those who have previously received awards are now demonstrating their impact. The Itsekiri Global Homecoming, for example, is being championed by recipients of the Royal Order of Iwere. This is the first time something like this is happening, and they have taken it upon themselves to make sure that it happens. We are also going to have royal representatives from different parts of Africa. You will see the richness and diversity of Itsekiri communities, whether they are poor or wealthy. We are talking about the Benin River axis and the culture that exists there. The camaraderie and even the friendly rivalry among the communities will all manifest through the Benin River Life series of events. The Minister of Culture, Arts and Tourism will be present and is very excited about the programme. The Minister of Communications will also be involved. There is an opportunity to work with the Iwere Kingdom to explore how telecommunications and communications infrastructure can be expanded in the riverine areas. So, the impact of His Majesty’s reach, words and actions is gradually coming into manifestation. The Itsekiri Kingdom is located in an area where there have been concerns about inter-ethnic relations. To what extent is the Olu addressing these challenges? These situations exist, but the beauty about the king we have is that he is at the forefront of addressing them. He does not take the back seat. He is involved in the key decisions and in determining how things should be driven. Interestingly, the main players in the area, the Itsekiri, Ijaw and Urhobo, have a very high level of mixed marriages. You cannot even define it. When you begin to look at issues around land and political territories, however, there is something else at play. It is power. What is important is that we engage at all levels and have a conversation that says what belongs to you should be yours. At the same time, we must recognise historical realities and understand that these things have always existed. There is no need to fight over them. The Warri axis, including the Warri Kingdom and neighbouring kingdoms, has been brought to its knees by ethnic nationality strife. There are also new players in the game who are making wealth from these divisions. The rule should be simple: if I have a glass house, I will not throw stones at your glass house because you will throw them back. I am happy for the wealth that is being created among everybody. At that point, there is nobody with sovereign power over violence. If the Urhobo are violent, if the Ijaw are violent and if the Itsekiri are violent, who pays the price? All of us will pay the price, because when there is violence, nobody makes money. Stability is important. Everybody should be able to make money and develop. Above all, there is a sovereign God who sees everything. The Itsekiri are known for their rich cultural heritage. What has sustained the culture over the centuries? That is a very interesting question. The simple answer is: water no get enemy. His Majesty has spoken about this philosophy before. He is not merely planning for the next cycle or even the next generation. He is laying institutional foundations for the next seven generations. He views leadership through the water cycle. Water flows. It does not get in anybody’s way. It nourishes, replenishes and empowers communities. The Itsekiri person is very close to water. We are a water people. If you observe our dances, particularly the way the women dance, there is a certain grace to it. It is like the movement of a duck on water. Even when there is a storm underneath, what you see is the graceful movement on the surface. When you see the men dancing, it can also look as if they are swimming. That is the gracious movement and respect for water, and it translates into many aspects of Itsekiri life and culture. One of the anniversary programmes focuses on the Itsekiri language. There have been concerns that the language could eventually become endangered. Do you share those concerns? Itsekiri is a minority ethnic nationality, and in Nigeria, the three major ethnic nationalities have their languages promoted extensively. If intentional action is not taken to protect minority languages, they will go into extinction. And this is not only an Itsekiri problem. It applies to many minority ethnic nationalities. If you travel across Nigeria, you hear the names of ethnic groups and their languages, many of which you may never have heard of before. We are fortunate as Itsekiri to have the visibility that we have. There are other ethnic nationalities with populations similar to ours that do not have that level of visibility. One thing the Itsekiri must do is to be intentional about preserving the language. That is why His Majesty has put the issue at the forefront. He is personally involved in celebrating children who are proficient in the language. But much more needs to be done. We need teacher training in the language. We need scholarships for people who want to become Itsekiri language teachers. We need to create jobs for them in our primary and secondary schools and, for those who are qualified, at the tertiary level. We also need researchers and fellows working on the language. We should create faculties or academic chairs dedicated to Itsekiri studies so that there can be further research and development of the language. It is a rich language. For a people with a history of more than 500 years, it is only logical that we should intentionally do more to preserve it for another 500 years and beyond. Warri is almost as famous as Nigeria itself, but the city still has significant infrastructure challenges. To what extent is the Olu pushing for the development and renewal of Warri? Warri was one of the early points of contact with the Portuguese. In the ancestral home of the Itsekiri, you also have what is believed to be one of the earliest Catholic churches in Nigeria, St Anthony’s Catholic Church, known locally as Satoni. We also have a long history of engagement with Europe and an ethnic nationality that produced what is arguably one of the earliest European-educated monarchs in West Africa, Dom Domingo. So, we have come a long way, even before the emergence of Nigeria. We are a nation, and we predate Nigeria, just as other great kingdoms, including the Benin Kingdom from which our monarch’s lineage comes, predate the modern Nigerian state. Now, moving to Warri as it is today, much of what you see is a consequence of the ethnic strife that has affected the city and its environs. We must commend the leadership of Governor Sheriff Oborevwori for helping to calm the situation that arose recently. What Warri needs most is peace among its peoples. Warri will always be a magnet for investment, particularly in the oil and gas sector. But there is another opportunity that we do not talk about enough: the blue economy. Warri has the potential to become a major hub for the blue economy, not just through industries that will operate there, but also through the development of human capital that can be exported from the entire Niger Delta region. Look at the Philippines. It is a major player in the maritime sector partly because it exports its citizens as human capital. You go to ships around the world and you find Filipinos. The Philippines does not have as large a population as Nigeria. It also has a coastline, just as Nigeria does. Yet Nigeria is not even doing five per cent of what the Philippines is doing in terms of exporting maritime human capital. Warri therefore has enormous potentialities. What we need is peace, stability, investment and deliberate development of the people and institutions that can turn that potential into wealth. Bight of Benin We are poor, but in reality, we are rich with our human resources. What can be done around the blue economy? When I say Warri, I am actually talking about Warri Kingdom, because you have a long stretch of ocean that goes across the Bight of Benin, and you have the various ethnic nationalities that are conversant with the creeks and those waters. There is a lot that can be done from that perspective. Now, to His Majesty, he sees the future of what we collectively, as a people, can make our homestead become. We can make it the greatest of all, because we have everything within us, both human and natural resources, to make all that happen. From that perspective, His Majesty engages his brother kings. It is from that perspective you see him engaging not just the local government authorities, but the state government authorities, the national and federal authorities, and, of course, with the permission of the Federal Government, you see him engaging even in cultural diplomacy with the rest of Africa and the rest of the world. All this is to bring attention to the potentialities in this area we call Warri Kingdom, which is not just Warri Kingdom itself, but even its environment and its neighbours, and to see what can be attracted to it. Cultural diplomacy You can see His Majesty undertaking a cultural diplomacy trip to Finland, because Finland is a forerunner in the education sector, where they have one of the most educated societies in the world. We want to learn from them. His Majesty wants to learn from them. He needs his people to be better educated. What have they done there that we can imbibe? You have His Majesty engaging with His Majesty in the United Kingdom, King Charles, to maintain those relationships. You have His Majesty undertaking trips to Canada and even to the United States, all this to engage technocrats and see history. We are blessed with our culture, which has gone on for so long. We are blessed currently with a visionary king, one who has a heart for his people. The ingredient needed right now is the belief or the execution of His Majesty’s vision for the Kingdom. The commitment to want to see that this Kingdom carries on being here for another 500 years by participating. And that is what His Majesty is trying to underline, even with this fifth coronation anniversary, by calling his children to come home and see your lands, see how beautiful it is. It has challenges, but the land needs you right now. That commitment from every son and daughter. The other ingredient that the Itsekiri need now is to see that their destiny is right in their hands. Nobody else can execute what they aspire for, which is good livelihood, peaceful living, the ability to express themselves, to acquire happiness, to have jobs and maintain an environment that is sustainable. Now, it is in their hands. It will also include a change in work ethic, which His Majesty is preaching, from a rent-seeking attitude to being a productive people, because our land is now, “Walk the land, work the land, bring out what you need.” We have seen your transition from the corporate sector to a notable titled person. Can you tell us what it feels like playing this role, and what are those responsibilities that the position placed or places on you? I would want to address that by starting off by saying Ogiame, I suppose, did not confer the title and the responsibility on me to come and just sit and wear the title as a chief. He knew and knows that I’m a technocrat. He knew and knows that I’m a leader. He knew and knows that I’m one that connects the nation. Interestingly, my Akuja, the appellation which he blessed me with, is Ajolaja, Ajolaja, the repairer of the town, the unifier, the one who makes things happen. Now, I am a chief of the Ogiame Court, with leadership amongst the chiefs. We are blessed to have the leadership of Chief Oma, who is the Ologbotsere of Warri Kingdom, who himself, yes, is aged, but a brilliant first-class technocrat. He is a first-class graduate, a technocrat, an engineer. He is a great leader to have on the chieftaincy train. Mine is to see how I add my own flair to the expression of the vision that His Majesty has laid for us. That said, I represent Itsekiri across the whole Kingdom, but I also have a people in those states where I’m also from, which is Ikara in the Iyashere lineage. So, you find that in all that, there have been challenges for my people, the Ikara people, in where you might call the Olugbo Forest Reserve area. There’s a lot that is going on in that angle, and thank God for Ogiame, who supports all that. Thank God for the leadership of the Iyashere of Warri Kingdom, Chief Johnson Asheruneghe, who also provides assistance to see that we can do what we need to do to get our rights done. It has been an interesting transition from being just a pure technocrat to now being a titled chief, because every Itsekiri that sees me dressed like this, or even sees me dressed traditionally, sees Ogiame. We are a direct representation of Ogiame, so we must carry ourselves accordingly, with the grace and dignity that the office demands. But even more so, they also demand good leadership. Ogiame is providing that for us, so we can only just reflect that and bring our own experience to bear. items.title: Démocratie à la Kiévienne : selon Zelensky des élections seraient «un tsunami» qui «fracturerait» le pays
items.description: « Si nous voulons detruire le pays, alors nous pouvons aller dans la direction d'elections dans ces temps de guerre », a declare Volodymyr Zelensky lors d'une rencontre avec des journalistes, selon des propos rendus publics ce 23 août, notamment par l'AFP qui etait presente. Cette derniere a souligne qu'il s'agissait de « la premiere depuis des mois ». Et d'evoquer une serie de « controverses politiques », dont le limogeage mi-juillet du « jeune et populaire ministre de la Defense », Mikhaïlo Fedorov. « Je pense que dans une guerre comme celle-ci, des elections en tant que telles sont un risque enorme », a encore affirme Volodymyr Zelensky, dont le mandat presidentiel a expire en mai 2024 , estimant que ces elections seraient un « tsunami » qui « fracturerait l'Ukraine ». Mikhaïlo Fedorov, un enieme ministre (janvier–juillet 2026) percu par le locataire du Palais Mariinsky comme un potentiel rival politique , a appele le 18 août dans une video ou il denonce la corruption a « restaurer un processus democratique » via des elections en Ukraine, un pays ou la loi martiale est en vigueur depuis l'eclatement du conflit russo-ukrainien en fevrier 2022. Video aux allures de clip de campagne, dans laquelle il a notamment pointe le sommet de l'establishment ukrainien, fustigeant « une crise de gouvernance systemique » et un « systeme qui se protege », « crains le changement » et « preferant la loyaute a la prise d'initiative ». « Il existe beaucoup de mythes sur les raisons pour lesquelles il n'est pas possible d'organiser des elections » « Nous devons repondre a une question fondamentale : comment l'etat doit-il fonctionner si la guerre dure des annees ? Et ensuite, que faire si la guerre se prolonge encore un an, deux ans, trois ans ? La Russie peut-elle effectivement obtenir le droit de decider quand les Ukrainiens pourront a nouveau elire leurs dirigeants ? Je suis convaincu que non », a-t-il lance , estimant que « la democratie ne peut etre l'otage de la Russie », avant d'appeler a « trouver un mecanisme legal, sûr et realiste qui permettra a l'Ukraine de retablir un processus democratique a part entiere, meme dans les conditions d'une guerre prolongee ». « Il existe beaucoup de mythes sur les raisons pour lesquelles il n'est pas possible d'organiser des elections, mais ces mythes peuvent etre rapidement dissipes afin de mettre en place ce processus », a-t-il par la suite declare le 21 août dans une interview-fleuve a la chaîne 24 Kanal, estimant qu'« il faut tenir toutes les elections ».

items.title: 2027: Akwa Ibom Stakeholders endorse Tinubu, Akpabio, Eno
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, critical stakeholders from the Ikot Ekpene Senatorial District of Akwa Ibom State, cutting across the All Progressives Congress (APC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and other political groups, have endorsed the re-election bids of President Bola Tinubu, Senate President Godswill Akpabio and Governor Umo Eno. The stakeholders announced their endorsement in a communique issued after a meeting of political leaders and other critical stakeholders from the district. The communique was read by the member representing Ukanafun/Oruk Anam Federal Constituency, Hon. Unyime Idem, and endorsed through a voice vote following a motion moved by Senator Emmanuel Ibokessien and seconded by Hon. Iboro Ekanem. According to a statement issued on Sunday by the Special Assistant to the President of the Senate on Media, Jackson Udom, the stakeholders reviewed the political situation in the state and assessed the contributions and performance of the three leaders before arriving at the decision. The communique read in part: “After reviewing the political situation and assessing the contributions and performance of the leaders and representatives, the stakeholders resolved to endorse them for another term in office in the 2027 General Elections. “Accordingly, the meeting endorsed President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for another term as President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria in the 2027 Presidential Election; Senator Godswill Obot Akpabio for another term as Senator representing Akwa Ibom North-West Senatorial District in the 2027 National Assembly Election; and Governor Umo Bassey Eno for another term as Governor of Akwa Ibom State in the 2027 Governorship Election.” Reacting to the endorsement, Akpabio attributed the development to what he described as the peaceful atmosphere in the state and the unity among political stakeholders. He said the endorsement demonstrated that opposition parties in the state were also supporting Tinubu’s administration. “The peace in the state has finally led to the opposition parties joining to declare that they all stand on the mandate of Mr President,” Akpabio said. He expressed appreciation for the endorsement, saying it showed that there was unity in Akwa Ibom State, particularly in the North-West Senatorial District. Akpabio also assured Tinubu and Eno of the district’s support during the elections. “I can assure President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Governor Umo Eno that the people of this district will give them 100 percent of the votes,” he said. The Senate President noted the presence of the Akwa Ibom State PDP Chairman, Hon. Aniekan Akpan, as well as some opposition candidates in the National Assembly elections at the meeting. He further appealed to political actors in the state to sustain peaceful coexistence and forgive one another in the interest of the state. “I will still continue to solicit for peaceful co-existence amongst us all. Whoever we have wronged in the course of our politicking, let us forgive and forget so that we can move in one direction and one voice during the electioneering and voting,” he said. Former Minister of Petroleum Resources, Don Etiebet; retired Deputy Inspector-General of Police, Udom Ekpoudom; Senators Aloysius Etuk, Emmanuel Ibokessien and Chris Ekpenyong, among other stakeholders, also pledged their support for the re-election of Tinubu, Akpabio and Eno. items.title: Riyad Mahrez va-t-il jouer au Maroc ? La star algérienne répond par un émoji
items.description: Ces derniers jours, une rumeur a beaucoup circulé sur les réseaux sociaux. La légende de l’équipe nationale d’Algérie, Riyad Mahrez , est annoncée dans un club marocain. Alors vrai ou faux ? Le Magic Man a répondu à la polémique. Il s’agit d’une annonce surprise, qui a choqué de nombreux fans algériens. L’ancien capitaine des Verts et ex-star de Manchester City sous le maillot d’un club marocain ? Un véritable sacrilège, estiment certains, bien que pour d’autres, le joueur soit libre de signer pour le club de son choix. Ce club marocain aurait des vues sur Riyad Mahrez Mais c'est quoi précisément cette histoire ? C’est dans le cadre du mercato estival, que le nom de Riyad Mahrez a été proposé à la direction du Wydad Casablanca, a dévoilé le média qatari WinWin, le 20 août dernier, citant ses propres sources. L’information n’a pas tardé à faire le tour des réseaux sociaux, suscitant une véritable polémique. Certains sont allés jusqu'à affirmer que le joueur algérien avait accepté une offre du club marocain. Mais l’ancienne star de Manchester City a vite mis un terme à ces bruits de couloir, et ce, via un simple emoji qu'il a posté en réponse à un article publié sur X. Le joueur de 35 ans, qui est actuellement sans club après la résiliation de son contrat avec Al Ahly (Arabie saoudite), a répondu à la polémique d’une manière on ne peut plus laconique, avec un simple emoji de désapprobation. Riyad Mahrez : un emoji qui vaut mille mots L’emoji, représentant un homme avec les deux bras croisés, signifie une réponse négative, voire un niet catégorique, ce qui semble mettre fin aux vues du Wydad et aux espoirs de bon nombre de ses supporters qui souhaitaient voir Mahrez porter le maillot de leur club. Il est à rappeler que Riyad Mahrez est courtisé par plusieurs clubs européens, notamment l’Olympique de Marseille et l’AS Rome, font savoir plusieurs sources. La star algérienne n’a cependant pas encore tranché et semble profiter de sa liberté. Pour rappel, l’international algérien a joué son dernier match avec la sélection algérienne contre la Suisse en 16 e de finale de la Coupe du monde 2026, le 3 juillet dernier à Vancouver. Les Verts ont perdu 2 à 0 et ont été éliminés de la compétition. Une triste fin pour l’ailier algérien qui a voulu terminer sa carrière en sélection sur une meilleure note. items.title: Éboulement à Dar-Es-Salam : le bilan passe à 22 morts
items.description: Le bilan de l’éboulement survenu ce dimanche à la décharge de Dar-Es-Salam, à Conakry, s’est alourdi. Alors qu’un précédent bilan faisait état de 18 à 20 décès, les opérations de recherche et de secours ont permis de retrouver deux nouvelles victimes, portant le nombre de morts à 22 à 14h20. La tragédie s’est produite lorsqu’une importante masse de déchets s’est brusquement effondrée, ensevelissant plusieurs personnes présentes sur le site. Les équipes de secours poursuivent les opérations de recherche, de dégagement et de fouille afin de retrouver d’éventuelles autres victimes, voire d’éventuels survivants coincés sous les décombres. La Protection civile reste pleinement mobilisée aux côtés des services compétents pour poursuivre les opérations de secours et apporter l’assistance nécessaire aux personnes affectées par ce drame. Le bilan demeure donc provisoire, les recherches étant toujours en cours sur le site.

items.title: Tinubu’s Group to Atiku: Leave foreign interference, campaign on policies
items.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka The Deputy National Leader (Southeast) of the Renewed Hope for Greater Nigeria (RHGN), Mazi Franklin Ngoforo, has urged former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to focus on convincing Nigerians about his plans for the country rather than seeking foreign intervention in Nigeria’s political affairs. Ngoforo made the call shortly after the flag-off of RHGN’s campaign activities for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in Jos, Plateau State, on Saturday. He argued that seeking external influence in domestic political matters could portray a presidential aspirant as unwilling to face democratic competition. According to him, any candidate seeking to govern Nigeria should focus on convincing Nigerian voters by presenting credible alternatives to the government’s approach to the country’s economic, security and developmental challenges. “If Atiku believes Nigerians do not want Tinubu, he should go to Nigerians and persuade them. If he believes Tinubu is legally unqualified, he should make his case under Nigerian law,” Ngoforo said. He urged Nigerians to reject political strategies that could expose the country’s electoral process to what he described as undue external influence. Ngoforo also called on voters to support Tinubu based on what he described as the administration’s record and ongoing development agenda, while urging RHGN members and supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation nationwide. He said the 2027 general election should provide Nigerians with an opportunity to exercise their sovereignty by choosing their president through the country’s democratic process. “The Nigerian President will not be elected in an American school, lobbying office or courtroom; he will be elected by Nigerians, on Nigerian soil, through the Nigerian ballot. “If there is a question about a Nigerian election, take it to the Nigerian courts and allow Nigerian law to determine it,” Ngoforo said. items.title: EPL: Maresca begins Man City reign with comeback win over Bournemouth
items.description: Manchester City made a winning start to life without Pep Guardiola as late goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol snatched a dramatic 2-1 victory against Bournemouth on Sunday in Enzo Maresca’s first Premier League game as the Spaniard’s replacement. Marcus Tavernier’s first half goal put Bournemouth ahead at the Etihad Stadium before City staged a pulsating fightback in the final minutes. Marc Guehi headed City’s equaliser with six minutes left before Gvardiol stroked in the stoppage-time winner. Guardiola won 20 trophies, including six Premier League titles, during a glorious decade with City. His reign started with a late win at home to Sunderland in 2016 and Maresca will hope his own narrow victory serves as the prelude to an equally successful spell. Maresca insists he can replicate Guardiola’s trophy haul if he is given time to handle the “big changes” at the club. City’s lacklustre 3-0 defeat against Arsenal in last weekend’s Community Shield raised questions about their ability to keep pace with the Premier League champions this season. For much of their top-flight opener, City were again short of inspiration in attack and cohesion at the back. But they found a way to dig out a result that allowed Maresca to breath a sigh of relief. It is a time of major upheaval at City, with Rodri, Bernardo Silva, John Stones, Nathan Ake and Tijjani Reijnders all leaving and Savinho set to join Tottenham. England midfielder Elliot Anderson has been Maresca’s only major signing and he was unimpressive before hobbling off in the second half. City are set to sign teenage Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a deal worth £86 million ($117 million), according to reports on Sunday. But more new recruits will be needed if City are to close the gap on Arsenal. – Critical decision – Maresca wasted little time emulating one aspect of Guardiola’s reign as he unveiled a curious starting line-up. The Italian picked six players who could be classed as defenders, with England centre-back Guehi deployed in midfield and Nico O’Reilly moved from his usual role on the left to a position closer to Erling Haaland in attack. Haaland shed his long blond hair on the eve of the new season, describing his close-cropped look as “new season, new trim”. The City striker, who starred for Norway at the World Cup, might have looked sharp, but his finishing was rusty when he somehow prodded wide from close-range after O’Reilly’s cross presented him with a golden opportunity. City were punished by an incisive counter from Bournemouth in the 26th minute. Evanilson’s perfectly weighted cross fizzed across the penalty area as City defenders Ruben Dias and Abdukodir Khusanov stood statuesque, allowing Tavernier time and space to stroke a composed finish past Gianluigi Donnarumma from six yards. City forwards Phil Foden and Antoine Semenyo struggled to link up effectively with Haaland, whose glancing header was clawed away by Djordje Petrovic. Guehi should have equalised immediately after the interval from Foden’s corner, but he surpassed Haaland’s woeful first half miss with an even worse header from virtually on the line. Moans from supporters underwhelmed by Maresca’s style of play were a constant soundtrack to his time at Chelsea. It must have alarmed City’s hierarchy to hear similar complaints from the stands before Maresca had even completed 90 minutes in charge. But Maresca made the critical decision to send on French playmaker Rayan Cherki and the move changed the course of the match. It was Cherki’s corner that arrowed towards Guehi in the 84th minute, presenting the defender with a chance that he headed past Petrovic in clinical fashion. And in stoppage-time, Cherki slipped a deft pass through the heart of the Bournemouth defence for Gvardiol to slot home as Maresca punched the air in delight. items.title: Joseph Kabila saisit la justice américaine contre les sanctions de Washington
items.description: Sanctionné par les États-Unis en avril 2026 pour son soutien présumé au M23 et à l’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC), l’ancien président congolais, Joseph Kabila, conteste ces accusations devant la justice américaine, selon des médias. Ses avocats dénoncent une décision fondée sur des éléments qu’ils jugent vagues et insuffisamment étayés. L’ancien président de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), Joseph Kabila, engage une bataille judiciaire aux États-Unis contre les sanctions qui lui ont été imposées en avril 2026. Dans une plainte de seize pages déposée au début du mois d’août 2026 devant un tribunal fédéral de Washington, l’ex-chef de l’État demande l’annulation de son inscription sur la liste de l’Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), une structure du département américain du Trésor chargée notamment de mettre en œuvre les sanctions économiques. Washington accuse Joseph Kabila d’avoir apporté un soutien financier et logistique à l’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC), coalition dont fait partie le M23. Les autorités américaines lui reprochent également d’avoir encouragé des militaires congolais à abandonner leurs rangs et d’avoir séjourné à Goma sous la protection du mouvement rebelle. Ces accusations sont fermement rejetées par l’ancien président, qui a dirigé la RDC de 2001 à 2019. Selon plusieurs sources, sa défense estime que les motifs avancés par l’administration américaine sont «vagues» et «arbitraires», et qu’ils ne reposent pas sur des éléments matériels suffisamment précis. Les avocats contestent notamment l’existence d’un transfert financier clairement identifié au profit de l’AFC. Ils soulignent aussi que les autorités américaines ne désignent aucun militaire congolais que Joseph Kabila aurait personnellement poussé à la désertion. Pour étayer leur argumentation, ses défenseurs rappellent également le rôle joué par l’ancien président dans la lutte contre le M23. Ils mettent notamment en avant l’offensive menée en 2013, lorsque les forces armées congolaises étaient parvenues à repousser le mouvement rebelle sous sa présidence. À travers cette procédure, Joseph Kabila demande donc à la justice fédérale américaine de revenir sur les sanctions prises à son encontre et de le retirer de la liste de l’OFAC. La démarche intervient dans un contexte où le M23 et l’AFC demeurent au centre des tensions sécuritaires et politiques qui secouent l’est de la RDC. En contestant officiellement les mesures américaines prises en avril 2026, l’ancien chef de l’État cherche ainsi à obtenir devant les tribunaux la levée de sanctions qu’il considère comme injustifiées, alors que les accusations américaines continuent de peser sur son activité politique. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Joseph Kabila saisit la justice américaine contre les sanctions de Washington est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: FG moves to ensure textbooks reach learners, tackles learning poverty
items.description: By Adesina Wahab LAGOS — The Federal Government has commenced steps to ensure that textbooks in Mathematics, English Language and other core subjects reach learners and are properly tracked and maintained as part of efforts to tackle learning poverty in Nigeria. The initiative is being implemented through a series of workshops organised by the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) in conjunction with the Federal Ministry of Education (FME) under the Human Capital Opportunities for Prosperity and Equity (HOPE-EDU) programme. The latest workshop, titled “Five-day Result Area One Regional Thematic Workshop on Book Supply Chain and Track ‘N’ Trace,” commenced in Lagos at the weekend. The workshop brought together education officers from Niger, Kogi, Kwara, Nasarawa, Benue, Plateau, Ekiti, Ondo, Ogun, Osun, Oyo and Lagos states, as well as the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja. HOPE-EDU is a Federal Government initiative supported by the World Bank to strengthen foundational learning through improved systems, institutional capacity and technical support. Under Results Area 1 (RA1), the programme is convening a series of regional thematic workshops on the Structured Pedagogy Package (SPP) Guidance and the Book Supply Chain and Track-and-Trace (BSC/TnT) System to strengthen the capacity of federal and state officials to support effective implementation. In her address, the Executive Secretary of UBEC, Dr Aisha Garba, commended the Federal Government and the Federal Ministry of Education for supporting the commission in implementing the HOPE-EDU programme. Garba said the workshops were designed to translate the programme’s objectives into practical support for states by equipping relevant federal and state officials with the knowledge, tools and systems required to strengthen implementation. She said the workshops would also demonstrate the government’s commitment to improving the quality and availability of teaching and learning materials while building transparent and accountable systems for education service delivery. “The engagement should therefore be positioned not simply as a technical workshop, but as an important step in translating HOPE-EDU’s investments and objectives into practical improvements at state and school levels, ultimately contributing to better teaching and learning outcomes for Nigerian children,” she said. Garba further stressed the importance of the November 15, 2026 deadline for states to demonstrate readiness for the programme. “By November 15, 2026, your states must demonstrate readiness. This is not negotiable. It is the gateway to unlocking the first round of programme disbursements and, more importantly, the future of our children,” she said. She noted that the participation of directors responsible for academic services, teacher professional development, monitoring and evaluation, procurement, and planning, research and statistics/electronic management information systems reflected the whole-of-system approach required for successful implementation. In her welcome remarks, the Programme Manager, Dr Aisha Abdul, said the HOPE-EDU programme became effective in February 2026, adding that implementation had focused on establishing the institutional, technical and operational foundations required to achieve its Programme Development Objective and Year 1 results. According to her, with the support of the World Bank team, technical experts and consultants, the programme had worked closely with states to lay the groundwork for reforms that the workshop would translate into action. Abdul said the Book Supply Chain and Track-and-Trace System was central to the programme’s commitment to ensuring that teaching and learning materials procured and financed through HOPE-EDU achieve a 1:1 pupil-to-book ratio in literacy and numeracy and reach classrooms intact and on time. She urged state delegations to participate actively in the workshop, resolve outstanding issues and leave with clear and actionable implementation plans. Abdul also drew participants’ attention to the November 15 deadline for submission of prerequisite evidence, urging states to use the workshop to resolve outstanding clarifications and avoid being caught unprepared. A representative of the Federal Ministry of Education, Mr Abdulgafar Otunola, said the ministry would continue its efforts to reposition the education sector. A World Bank consultant, Gerard Peart, said the bank was supporting HOPE-EDU within the context of the Universal Basic Education programme. He identified quality, access and system strengthening as critical to making primary education functional, noting that learning poverty remained a major challenge in the sector. “One of the major problems confronting primary education in Nigeria is learning poverty occasioned by overcrowded classrooms, lack of textbooks, teaching and learning materials. If we want to get more from basic education, textbooks must be available in the classrooms and in required quantity,” Peart said. items.title: Hina Javed murder case: Rawalpindi court sends husband, servant on 3-day physical remand
items.description: RAWALPINDI: A duty magistrate in Rawalpindi on Sunday remanded the husband and servant of Hina Javed in police custody for three days in her murder case. Hina was found dead in the washroom of her apartment in Askari Apartments in Rawalpindi on Thursday evening. Police said that the body bore signs of torture, with a wire fastened around her neck and tied to the shower rod. They detained her husband and a servant in relation to the case. Today, the suspects were produced before a duty magistrate by police, who sought their remand for further investigation. The court granted the Civil Lines police their three-day physical remand, directing authorities to submit a progress report after the remand’s completion. The FIR A first information report of the case was registered on Aug 20 at the Civil Lines police station under Sections 302 (premeditated murder) and 34 (common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code. The complainant, Hina’s brother, Fahid Javed, alleged in the FIR that his sister had been murdered by her husband, her father-in-law and their domestic servant. Fahid told police that he received a telephone call from his sister’s father-in-law at 6:53pm on Thursday, informing him of an emergency at their residence. He said he rushed to the apartment with other family members and arrived there at 7:23pm. He claimed that when he arrived at the residence, he found his sister’s body in the bathroom. The complainant further alleged that his sister had been subjected to “severe torture and mistreatment” by her husband. He also claimed that she might have been administered a poisonous substance before her death. In his complaint, Fahid said Hina had married the suspect in November 2025. An initial postmortem examination indicated a strangulation mark around her neck, an injury below her right lip and bleeding. On Sunday, police sources told Dawn the cause of death could be ascertained with finality after the Punjab Forensic Science Agency’s (PFSA) report was received. The sources said the role of Hina’s father-in-law in the case was also yet to be determined and that he was being questioned and asked not to leave the city. Meanwhile, they added, a seven-member team, headed by Rawalpindi Senior Superintendent of Police (Investigation) Saifullah had been formed to investigate the case. The sources also said that mobile phones of the victim and three of her family members had been taken into custody for investigation.

items.title: Ayyoub Bouaddi devrait signer à Manchester City pour 100 millions d’euros
items.description: Ayyoub Bouaddi est tout proche de devenir un nouveau joueur de Manchester City. Le milieu de terrain marocain de Lille a trouvé un accord avec le club anglais, qui aurait également obtenu le feu vert du LOSC pour finaliser l’opération. Selon le spécialiste du mercato Fabrizio Romano, le transfert est désormais « bouclé ». Un accord aurait été trouvé entre Lille et Manchester City pour une opération pouvant atteindre 100 millions d’euros, bonus compris. Fabrizio Romano indique également que Bouaddi avait déjà trouvé un accord sur les conditions personnelles de son contrat avec Manchester City en juillet dernier. Le club anglais aurait désormais obtenu l’autorisation de Lille pour finaliser la signature du jeune milieu marocain et l’intégrer à son projet. Cette opération confirme l'intérêt considérable suscité par Bouaddi, qui s'apprête à franchir un nouveau cap dans sa jeune carrière en rejoignant l'un des clubs les plus ambitieux du football européen. Si le montant annoncé de 100 millions d’euros, bonus compris, se confirme, l’arrivée de Bouaddi à Manchester City constituerait l’un des transferts les plus importants de ce mercato. Le joueur de Lille devrait ainsi découvrir la Premier League et évoluer sous les couleurs de Manchester City, avec l’ambition de s’imposer progressivement dans l’effectif mancunien. Pour le football marocain, cette arrivée représente également une nouvelle vitrine. Bouaddi, présenté comme l’un des grands talents de la nouvelle génération des Lions de l’Atlas, pourrait désormais poursuivre son développement au sein d’un projet de très haut niveau. Après plusieurs semaines de négociations, Ayoub Bouaddi semble donc avoir fait son choix : Manchester City se rapproche désormais concrètement de sa signature. items.title: NGE Conference: Onaiyekan, Mbah, Osigwe, others to speak in Enugu
items.description: The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has announced that its 2026 All Nigeria Editors Conference (ANEC) will hold at the International Conference Centre (ICC), Enugu, on September 24 and 25. More than 500 editors from across the country, alongside other distinguished guests, are expected at the annual conference, which is the flagship gathering of the Guild. The 2026 edition will focus on critical national and global issues, particularly the role of the media in strengthening democracy ahead of the 2027 general elections. The theme of the conference is “The Ballot, the Media and the Task of Keeping Democracy Alive,” while the sub-theme is “When Lies Look Real: Detecting and Debunking AI Disinformation Before, During and After Election.” His Royal Majesty, Igwe Nnaemeka Alfred Achebe, the Obi of Onitsha, will chair the conference. In a statement signed by the NGE President and General Secretary, Eze Anaba and Onuoha Ukeh, respectively, the Guild said the conference would provide an opportunity for media leaders and other stakeholders to examine the challenges confronting democracy and the media’s role in safeguarding credible elections, public trust and democratic values. Former Catholic Archbishop of Abuja, Cardinal John Onaiyekan, is scheduled to deliver the keynote address at the opening ceremony on September 24 at 2pm. Also on the first day, Prof. Auwal Yadudu of the Faculty of Law, Bayero University, Kano, will speak on “Public Trust, Electoral Justice and Democratic Stability,” while Enugu State Governor, Dr Peter Mbah, will address the conference. Ombudsman and Public Protector of ThisDay Newspapers, Kayode Komolafe, and veteran journalist and civil rights campaigner, Owei Lakemfa, will jointly present a paper titled “Reporting Terrorism Without Becoming a Tool for Terrorists.” The second day will feature a presentation by the immediate past President of the Nigerian Bar Association, Mazi Afam Osigwe, on “Election Petitions in the Digital Age: Independence, Evidence, BVAS and the Courts.” His presentation is scheduled for 9am. Deputy Vice-Chancellor of Paul University, Awka, Prof. Chinyere Okunna, will speak on “Neutrality, Professionalism and Election Security in Democratic Governance.” Founder and Chief Medical Director of Save A Life Hospital, Port Harcourt, Dr Richard Okoye, will address the issue of journalists’ welfare and wellbeing in a presentation titled “The Human Side of Journalism: Managing Stress, Deadlines and Personal Wellbeing.” Professor of Journalism and Emerging Media at Kennesaw State University, Georgia, United States, Prof. Farooq A. Kperogi, will examine the conference’s sub-theme on detecting and debunking artificial intelligence-generated disinformation before, during and after elections. The second day will also feature an Executive Session at 12:30pm, during which editors will engage governors, political party leaders and heads of government parastatals on issues of national importance. The Guild said the conference would provide a platform for editors and other stakeholders to explore pathways for advancing democratic governance, promoting national development and strengthening nation-building through responsible and responsive journalism. It added that the gathering would enable media leaders to interrogate emerging threats to democracy and develop strategies for ensuring that the media continues to play a critical role in promoting credible elections, public accountability and democratic stability. items.title: JoyNews-Republic Bank Habitat Fair finale turns homeownership dreams into real possibilities
items.description: The JoyNews-Republic Bank Habitat Fair 2026 is close to ending at the Achimota Retail Centre, after three days of conversations, exhibitions and practical opportunities for people looking to build, buy, finance or improve their homes. The final day of the mini-fair on Sunday, August 23, attracted patrons who moved from stand to stand, engaging exhibitors and exploring solutions across Ghana’s housing and construction sector. Held under the theme “Dream it. Explore it. Own it,” the fair was designed to take homeownership beyond aspiration by putting prospective homeowners in direct contact with businesses and professionals who could help them take the next step. From building materials and construction solutions to home financing, property development, furnishing and home improvement, exhibitors used the three-day event to showcase products and services while responding to questions from visitors. For many patrons, the experience was as much about getting answers as it was about looking at products. Visitors had the opportunity to compare options, speak directly with industry players, and better understand some of the decisions involved in building or owning a home. The strong interest continued through the weekend despite intermittent rain in Accra on Saturday and Sunday, with patrons still making their way to the fairgrounds to engage exhibitors. The fair brought together a range of companies and service providers across the housing value chain, including Akwaaba Building Materials, Lesh Fortune Ltd, MTN, Door Masters, Ayuda, Western Vilas, CTECHI Ghana LTD, Saint-Gobain Ghana, Sintex Tank, Interplast and Clifton Homes. The initiative was organised in partnership with Republic Bank, under its brand promise “We’re the one for you!”, and powered by Drive EV GH. As the exhibition comes to an end, the emphasis remains on helping prospective homeowners move from simply imagining the home they want to practical decisions about how to achieve it. For some visitors, that could mean finding the right building materials. For others, it could mean understanding financing options, exploring property opportunities or identifying professionals who can help turn an idea into a plan. That practical connection between the dream of owning a home and the steps required to achieve it has been at the heart of the 2026 Habitat Fair. The conversations started at the fair are expected to continue in homes, offices, construction sites and financial institutions, where many of the decisions about Ghana’s next generation of homes will ultimately be made.

items.title: FG offers ₦5m grant to young Nigerian entrepreneurs – how to apply
items.description: The Federal Government (FG) has announced grants of up to ₦5 million for young Nigerian entrepreneurs through the NiYA × Cascador Founders Programme, a four-week initiative designed to support business development, investment readiness, pitch preparation and mentorship. The programme is being implemented by the Federal Ministry of Youth Development in partnership with Cascador and Sapphital, with 20 young founders set to be selected for the pilot cohort. At the end of the programme, the eight top-performing founders will be eligible to receive up to ₦5 million each in non-dilutive funding from Cascador. The selected funding recipients will also receive an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solution to help improve business management, structure and growth. The programme is designed to help early-stage entrepreneurs develop stronger business fundamentals, improve their investment readiness and learn how to present their businesses effectively to potential investors. Participants will take part in training sessions, mentorship, virtual engagements and a final Pitch Day, where their progress and business ideas will be assessed. However, selection into the 20-member cohort does not automatically guarantee funding. Only the eight top-performing participants will be considered for the funding, subject to the programme’s assessment and funding conditions. Applicants are also required to provide accurate information during the application process. The organisers reserve the right to verify information submitted and disqualify applicants who provide false or misleading details. How to apply Young Nigerian entrepreneurs interested in the programme can apply through the NiYA × Cascador Founders Programme application portal. Applicants should create a profile, provide the required personal and business information and complete the application form before submitting it for consideration. The programme is powered by the Federal Ministry of Youth Development, with Cascador serving as the funder/donor and Sapphital as the implementing partner Successful applicants will be expected to commit to the full four-week programme and actively participate in the training, mentorship and pitch activities. items.title: From street to street, APC mobilises Eti-Osa East LCDA ahead of 2027
items.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Eti-Osa East Local Council Development Area (LCDA), Lagos, on Sunday inaugurated coordinators of the Kadiri Obafemi Hamzat (KOH) Consolidated Renewed Hope 2027. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that KOH was initiated to strengthen grassroots mobilisation and galvanise support for the APC ahead of the 2027 general elections. Mr Ismal Azeez, the Lagos State Board of Trustees Chairman of KOH Consolidated Renewed Hope 2027, described the exercise as a new beginning and a strong demonstration of the party’s commitment to securing victory for its governorship candidate and the party in the coming elections. Azeez, the former Vice Chairman of Eti-Osa East LCDA, said the mobilisation would secure victory for President Bola Tinubu’s second term, Dr Kadri Hamzat as the next governor of Lagos State, and all APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. According to him, the inauguration is designed to deepen grassroots engagement and ensure that the vision and programmes of the KOH team reach every ward, household and community within Eti-Osa East LCDA. He urged the newly inaugurated coordinators to see their appointments as a call to service rather than merely as titles. “Leadership is not about titles alone, but about responsibility, service, loyalty and commitment to our great party,” he said. “We charge the coordinators to work collectively towards victory for the APC at all levels. The success of the party will depend largely on effective mobilisation, communication, unity and commitment,” he said. The BoT chairman said the coordinators had been entrusted with the responsibility of taking the values and vision of the KOH team to every ward and household in the LCDA. He further urged them to build an inclusive political structure where youths and women were fully carried along and where committed party members were given opportunities to contribute meaningfully. The Elejigbo of Langbasa Land, Oba Azeez Badiru, represented by the Aro of Langbasa, High Chief Rufai Agbomabini, also charged the newly inaugurated coordinators to intensify efforts to encourage greater youth participation in the 2027 elections. Badiru commended the organisers for promoting youth involvement and urged young people to participate actively in the electoral process. “We appeal to the youths to come out en masse and cast their votes for President Tinubu for continuity,” he said. Also speaking, the State Coordinator of KOH, Mr Sanni Bamgbola, tasked the newly inaugurated team with delivering stronger grassroots mobilisation and ensuring victory for the APC in both the presidential and governorship elections. Bamgbola said youths had been actively carried along across communities, adding that many were already participating in the party’s mobilisation and campaign activities. He said the KOH initiative was focused on communicating the achievements of the Tinubu administration and promoting its policies and programmes at the grassroots. According to him, the movement is also aimed at consolidating the achievements of the present Lagos State administration under Gov.Babajide Sanwo-Olu through the incoming administration of Hamzat. “We assure the President that Lagos youths are ready to cast their votes for him come 2027,” Bamgbola said. A community leader in Ajah, Chief Kazeem Odunlami, commended Azeez for facilitating the inauguration, describing it as an important step towards strengthening grassroots participation and youth inclusion. Odunlami expressed optimism that increased political participation would ensure that communities in Eti-Osa East received greater representation in government. “We want our people here to become commissioners, special advisers and other top officials. That is why we are putting more effort into canvassing votes for the APC at the next elections,” he said. Mr Abiodun Adeyemi, in his remarks on behalf of the newly inaugurated coordinators, thanked the party leaders for the confidence reposed in the team. Adeyemi pledged that the coordinators would work diligently, mobilise effectively and remain committed to securing victory for the APC in the community in the 2027 general elections. items.title: Bamiri chief commissions KG block, guest house to boost education and revenue
items.description: The Chief of Bamiri and Tuntuhene of the Techiman Traditional Council, Nana Asare Baffour II, has commissioned two major development projects in the community as part of this year’s Yam Festival celebrations. The projects, comprising a modern Kindergarten (KG) block and a guest house, are intended to improve the safety and learning environment for children while generating revenue to support the community’s development needs. The commissioning ceremonies were attended by traditional leaders, community members and school authorities. New KG block to improve safety and learning environment The new KG facility was constructed partly in response to concerns over the safety of children at the old school premises, where pupils were exposed to traffic risks while playing or crossing nearby roads. Nana Asare Baffour II said the safety of children was a major motivation for providing the new facility. “I could not sit back and watch our children risk their lives every day just to get an education,” he said. “This Kindergarten block is my contribution to their safety and to the improvement of education in Bamiri. Every child deserves a secure environment to learn and grow.” The Headmistress of the school, Gifty Adjei Sarpong, who received the facility on behalf of the school, expressed appreciation to the chief for the intervention. She said the project had come at a critical time and had addressed the school’s longstanding accommodation challenges. “This facility has come at the right time. It has solved our accommodation problems and given our children a safe space to learn,” she said. Madam Sarpong, however, appealed for additional support for teaching and learning materials to enable the school to make full use of the new facility. Guest house to generate funds for development The chief also commissioned a newly constructed guest house, which is expected to generate revenue for the community. Located within the Techiman township, the facility is intended to accommodate visitors, travellers and business people who patronise the area. Proceeds from the guest house will be channelled into community development projects to reduce Bamiri’s reliance on external support. Nana Asare Baffour II said the facility formed part of a broader strategy to make the community more financially self-sufficient. “We cannot depend on handouts forever,” he said. “This Guest House will generate revenue for the community, which will in turn support other developmental initiatives. It is about building a sustainable future for Bamiri.” Bamiri’s development Bamiri has in recent years developed from a predominantly farming community into a growing township with a population of more than 5,000. The community now has several basic social and economic amenities, including a water supply system, police station, CHPS compound, fabrication company, technical institute, public place of convenience and a gari processing factory. The addition of the KG block and guest house is expected to further strengthen the community’s infrastructure and support its development ambitions. The projects were commissioned as part of this year’s Yam Festival, which attracted hundreds of residents and visitors to Bamiri.

C’était en présence du Directeur national adjoint des sports, du président du Comité national olympique et sportif de Guinée, de l’ambassadeur du Japon en Guinée, d’honorables députés et de plusieurs autres invités. Pays hôte pour la troisième fois consécutive, la Guinée s’est illustrée en remportant plusieurs médailles d’or devant son public, grâce à Mama Aïssata Camara (Kata individuel female cadet), Ramatoulaye Hawil (Kata individuel junior dame), Yaya Touré (Kumite individuel cadet homme -70 kg), Ansoumane Conté (Kumite individuel cadet homme +70 kg), Thierno Oumar Sow ( Kumite individuel junior homme -68 kg), Alpha Oumar Barry (Kumite individuel male -52 kg), Alhassane Sylla (Or, Kumite individuel U21 homme -67 kg), Mariama Penda Diallo Kumite individuel junior dames +66 kg), Moussa (Kumite individuel junior male -76 kg). Mais le Sénégal s’est adjugé le Grand Prix grâce à une performance remarquable, couronnée notamment par la médaille d’or du Team Kata senior. Président de l’Union des Fédérations Africaines de Karaté (UFAK), Souleymane Gaye n’a pas caché sa satisfaction à l’issue de l’événement. Il a félicité la Fédération guinéenne pour avoir accepté d’organiser une troisième édition consécutive, alors qu’aucun autre pays ne s’était porté candidat. « Nous sommes très satisfaits. C’est la troisième fois consécutive que Me Cheick Condé organise ce championnat en tant que président de la Région Ouest 1. En principe, cette année, on aurait dû être dans un autre pays. Faute de candidat déclaré, le président Condé a pris sur lui pour organiser ce championnat ». Pour le dirigeant africain, la réussite dépasse le cadre sportif. Il salue la mobilisation, le niveau des athlètes, mais aussi le travail réalisé autour de la formation des arbitres et des experts de la Fédération mondiale de karaté (WKF). « Pour l’UFAK, c’est une satisfaction pleine par rapport à l’organisation, à la mobilisation générale. Bravo à tous les athlètes, aux médaillés, aux arbitres qui ont réussi leurs examens ainsi qu’aux experts dépêchés par l’UFAK et la WKF pour accompagner le développement du karaté ». À la tête de la Fédération guinéenne de karaté et président de la Région Ouest 1, Me Cheick Condé retient avant tout les progrès enregistrés par les différentes sélections. Il s’est réjoui du retour de la Gambie, absente lors des deux précédentes éditions, estimant que cette présence illustre les efforts entrepris pour redynamiser le karaté dans la sous-région. « J’ai une bonne impression de réussite et de voir le karaté avancer. La Gambie, qui n’était pas présente lors des deux précédentes éditions, est revenue avec une bonne équipe et une belle image ». Le responsable guinéen a également rendu hommage au président de l’UFAK pour son engagement auprès des fédérations nationales. « C’est un salut qui revient au président de l’UFAK, qui prend son bâton de pèlerin pour passer de région en région, appeler chaque président pour se mettre en mouvement afin de relever le défi d’être le meilleur sur le plan continental ». Grande nation de cette 6ᵉ édition, le Sénégal repart de Conakry avec le trophée du Grand Prix. Une domination que résume parfaitement Shaibou Al Rahmane, l’un des artisans du succès sénégalais : « Nous avons bossé dur pour arriver jusqu’au sommet. Ce n’est que le début et le meilleur reste à venir. Le secret, c’est le travail : toujours travailler, encore travailler et tout le temps travailler. Nous sommes venus au nombre de quatre athlètes et nous avons une réussite totale avec sept médailles, dont six en or et une en argent ». Au-delà des résultats, cette 6ᵉ édition confirme la capacité de la Guinée à accueillir des compétitions internationales de karaté. Entre une organisation saluée par les instances africaines, une forte mobilisation du public et des performances encourageantes des athlètes guinéens, Conakry renforce son statut de place forte du karaté dans la Région Ouest 1. Sadjo Bah L’article Championnat d’Afrique de karaté : Conakry réussit son pari, le Sénégal décroche le Grand Prix de la Région Ouest 1 est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: NSMQ 2026: Yaa Asantewaa Girls’ going ‘beck’ to Tanoso after Bishop Herman deals them early exit
items.description: The “Adeshyeɛ” couldn’t rule. Returning Yaa Asantewaa Girls’ SHS’ much-anticipated comeback to the National Science and Maths Quiz has ended in disappointment after Bishop Herman College dealt them a decisive blow in the battle for a place in the One-Eighth Stage. Bishop Herman dominated from the opening round, taking an early 24–11 lead over Yaa Asantewaa Girls’, with debutants Dabala SHTS on 15. The Kpando-based school stretched its advantage to 30 points in Round Two, while Yaa Asantewaa Girls’ managed just 10. Dabala remained within reach on 21. Bishop Herman continued to pull away in Round Three, reaching 37 points, while Dabala moved to 24 and Yaa Asantewaa Girls’ struggled at 14. By Round Four, the writing was firmly on the wall. Bishop Herman had opened a commanding 44–24 lead over Yaa Asantewaa Girls’, with Dabala on 34. The final round offered little change to the order. Bishop Herman finished on 47 points to secure the One-Eighth Stage ticket, followed by Dabala SHTS with 37 points. Yaa Asantewaa Girls’ ended the contest on 27 points, bringing their return to the national stage to an abrupt end. For the Tanoso Girls, the royal comeback has ended before the One-Eighth Stage, and the “Adeshyeɛ” are going “beck” to Tanoso. Dinar algérien : l’euro gagne du terrain sur les marchés parallèle et officiel
items.description: Les choses bougent pour les principales devises sur le marché noir en Algérie. La tendance est à la hausse désormais pour l’euro , alors que son cours avait nettement baissé à la mi-août. Le dollar américain a enregistré quant à lui une nette baisse. Marché des devises en Algérie : l’euro en hausse, le dollar chute Le 12 août dernier, un euro était coté chez les cambistes du Square Port-Saïd d’Alger à 275 dinars algériens l’unité. 11 jours après, soit ce dimanche 23 août, la monnaie unique européenne gagne du terrain, mais sans pour autant dépasser la barre des 280 dinars. En effet, au Square Port-Saïd, véritable plaque tournante du marché parallèle des devises en Algérie, un euro est proposé aujourd’hui à 276,50 dinars algériens l’unité, soit une hausse de 1,5 dinar en 11 jours. Bien que l'évolution du marché noir des devises soit difficile à cerner ou à prévoir, le durcissement de l’attribution de l’allocation touristique de 750 euros, nécessitant désormais une carte bancaire internationale, pourrait avoir contribué à faire monter les cours de l’euro. Mais contrairement à la devise européenne, le dollar américain a quant à lui pris un sacré coup en cette deuxième moitié du mois d'août. Alors qu’il était coté à près de 240 dinars l’unité le 12 août dernier, le billet vert recule fortement ce 23 août. Les cambistes du Square Port-Saïd proposent ce dimanche la devise américaine à 236,50 dinars algériens, soit une baisse de 2,5 dinars algériens par rapport à son cours du 12 août dernier (239 dinars l’unité). L’euro franchit la barre des 155 dinars sur le marché officiel Cette montée de l’euro et la baisse du dollar américain interviennent alors que les vacances d'été touchent à leur fin pour beaucoup d’Algériens de l’étranger, notamment de France, venus passer quelques jours en Algérie et qui rentrent désormais en France pour la rentrée scolaire. Du côté de la Banque d’Algérie, le dollar américain était à 132,85 dinars algériens à la vente vendredi 21 août contre 132,77 DZD la veille. Pour la monnaie unique européenne, elle a gagné du terrain, en franchissant la barre des 155 dinars l’unité vendredi 21 août. Selon les cotations de la Banque d’Algérie, elle s’affichait à 155,08 dinars algériens l’unité contre 153,47 dinars le 17 août, soit un gain de près de 2 DA en cinq jours. L’article Dinar algérien : l’euro gagne du terrain sur les marchés parallèle et officiel est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Camp vacances Faso Mêbo à Fada N’Gourma : La promotion « Toyiro» s’engage à demeurer une graine d’espérance
items.description: La première cohorte du Camp vacances Faso Mêbo pour le compte de la 6 e Région militaire a effectué, samedi 22 août 2026, sa sortie officielle. Baptisée « Toyiro», qui signifie « l’avenir vous appartient » en langue nationale Bwamu, elle s’est engagée à demeurer une graine d’espérance. Après dix jours de formation civique et patriotique, la première cohorte de l'initiative présidentielle « Camp vacances Faso Mêbo » pour le compte de la 6 e Région militaire a effectué sa sortie officielle, samedi 22 août 2026, à Fada N'Gourma. Au nombre de 525 et âgés de 10 à 15 ans, les jeunes campeurs ont été formés, durant leur séjour, au civisme, au patriotisme, à la discipline, à la solidarité et au vivre ensemble, sans oublier les exercices d'éducation physique, militaire et sportive. Leur quotidien était rythmé également par les travaux de Faso Mêbo, notamment la confection de pavés, mais aussi par des séances de plantation d'arbres. Le lieutenant-colonel Aboubacar Dadijan, commandant la 6e Région militaire et parrain régional de l’évènement, a félicité les encadreurs et les formateurs pour le travail « titanesque » accompli. S’adressant aux parents des campeurs, le représentant du directeur général de Faso Mêbo, le sous-lieutenant Inoussa Koutou, les a exhortés à poursuivre la mission. « Chers parents, les valeurs que vos enfants ont apprises ici ne doivent pas rester au Camp. Faso Mebô a semé, les encadreurs ont arrosé. A vous de faire pousser et grandir cette semence », a-t-il lancé. items.title: «Où sont les faits ?» : dans une tribune, Xénia Fedorova interpelle Jean-Noël Barrot
items.description: « On peut ecarter une journaliste. On ne peut pas ecarter indefiniment les questions auxquelles on ne veut pas repondre ». Dans une tribune , parue ce 23 août, l'ancienne directrice de RT France, Xenia Fedorova, sous le feu des critiques des pro-Kiev depuis sa reapparition sur des medias du groupe Bollore, est revenue sur la procedure d'expulsion prise a son encontre fin juillet et les rejets de ses referes. Deux decisions, du tribunal administratif de Paris – notamment motivees par le fait que Fedorova se trouvait a l'etranger lorsqu'elle a ete visee par l'arrete – que le ministre francais des Affaires etrangeres, Jean-Noel Barrot, n'a pas manque de monter en epingle dans une tribune parue mi-août dans les colonnes du Monde – quotidien subventionne qui avait salue cette expulsion –, estimant que ce « cas […] illustre la menace d'ingerence a laquelle nous sommes confrontes ». «Pour un lecteur non juriste, cet enchaînement peut donner l'impression que les juridictions ont confirme, ou a tout le moins valide, les accusations d'ingerence formulees contre moi. Or les deux decisions n'ont precisement pas statue sur le fond de ces accusations », a pour sa part souligne Xenia Fedorova. « Aucun juge n'a etabli que mon expulsion etait legale ni que j'aurais execute des "operations de destabilisation pilotees par le Kremlin" », a ajoute celle dont les comptes bancaires ont egalement ete geles, evoquant une precision « essentielle » avant de rappeler que Barrot a lui-meme declare dans sa tribune qu'«une opinion n'est pas une ingerence» et « peut etre exprimee librement et sans crainte ». « Transformer certaines opinions en soupcons » « Quelle intervention etrangere ai-je executee ? Quelle cyberattaque ai-je organisee ? Quels faux comptes ai-je diriges ? Quelle campagne clandestine ai-je pilotee ? De quelles instructions du Kremlin aurais-je ete destinataire ? Ou sont les faits ? La tribune du ministre ne repond a aucune de ces questions », peut-on lire dans la tribune de Fedorova, qui pointe du doigt celle du « gouvernement francais ». « Il s'inquiete du fait que, meme s'il peut trouver un pretexte pour m'expulser en urgence absolue, il devra tot ou tard se confronter aux faits et aux preuves qu'il ne peut pas produire », a estime la journaliste. Cette derniere voit dans ces accusations d'« ingerence russe » fusants a tout va, plus qu' une « obsession » qui « detourne l'attention » politiquement, mais egalement comme « une categorie politique de plus en plus extensible » qui « permet de transformer certaines opinions en soupcons, certains contradicteurs en relais d'une puissance etrangere et, demain peut-etre, certains resultats electoraux en produits de manipulations venues de Moscou ». Une allusion a peine voilee a l'annulation, fin 2024, du premier tour de l'election presidentielle en Roumanie.

items.title: Sofiane Boufal se rapproche d’un retour en Espagne
items.description: Sofiane Boufal pourrait retrouver le championnat espagnol. L’international marocain est suivi de près par le Deportivo La Corogne, qui cherche à renforcer son secteur offensif durant ce mercato estival. Selon le quotidien espagnol La Opinión A Coruña, les dirigeants du club galicien ont inscrit le nom de Boufal parmi les joueurs susceptibles de renforcer leur attaque. Le Deportivo pourrait passer à l’action dans les prochains jours. Cette piste intervient après une demi-saison encourageante du Marocain au Havre, où il a tenté de relancer sa carrière et de retrouver son meilleur niveau. À 32 ans, Boufal présente également l’avantage d’être libre de tout engagement depuis cet été. Une situation qui pourrait faciliter son arrivée dans un nouveau club, puisqu’aucune indemnité de transfert ne serait nécessaire. Le Deportivo La Corogne ne serait toutefois pas le seul club espagnol à surveiller la situation du joueur. D’après les mêmes informations, un autre club espagnol serait également intéressé par ses services. Le club galicien souhaite de son côté renforcer ses ambitions après avoir notamment recruté cet été l’attaquant gabonais Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang. Un retour en Espagne constituerait une nouvelle étape dans la carrière de Boufal, qui connaît déjà le football espagnol. Le Marocain avait notamment porté les couleurs du Celta Vigo entre 2018 et 2019, sous forme de prêt en provenance de Southampton. La saison dernière, Boufal a disputé 17 rencontres de Ligue 1 avec Le Havre, inscrivant un but et délivrant quatre passes décisives.
